name: goldratt-toc
label: TOC: пять фокусирующих шагов
instructions: Diagnose the current system constraint and its effect on the complete verified result. Use the five focusing steps: identify, exploit, subordinate, elevate and repeat. Do not equate local utilization or a large queue with proof of the bottleneck. Preserve evidence, budget and the distinction between measurements, calculations, hypotheses and missing data.

procedure: Define the system boundary, useful verified result, demand, flow and protective metrics in common units and period.
Map stages, queues, rework, waiting, shared resources and external dependencies before choosing a constraint.
Identify a candidate constraint by observation, mechanism and expected system-level effect; test a plausible alternative when data permits.
Exploit the constraint by removing avoidable losses, defects, waiting, unnecessary switching and work without demand.
Subordinate release, priorities, input preparation and local KPIs to the constraint while protecting sustainable flow rather than maximum utilization.
Elevate only after exploit and subordinate are insufficient, comparing total effect, cost, delay, reversibility and the next likely constraint.
Define a measurable experiment with baseline, success and stop conditions, then repeat identify after the constraint moves.
preconditions: The useful system result and its protective constraints can be stated explicitly.
Observations, calculations, hypotheses and missing data can be distinguished.
inputs: Goal, demand, flow stages and existing obligations.
Queue, latency, attempt, compute and verification data when available.
Current budgets, failure records and previous interventions.
contract.output: A role-required result with the system goal, evidence-backed constraint candidate, exploit-subordinate-elevate plan, first measurable experiment and the condition for repeating diagnosis. Do not invent thresholds, capacity or effect sizes.
stop_criteria: Stop when one next measurable intervention and its system-level decision rule are explicit.
Stop with a preliminary diagnosis and measurement plan when evidence cannot distinguish plausible constraints.
examples: Success: after the upper bound is certified, work concentrates on the missing lower bound instead of increasing the speed of already completed constructions.
Failure: one busy reviewer is not declared the bottleneck from utilization alone; queue age, input starvation and alternative explanations are checked first.
